item.title: Permission to Build: The Vote That Split the A.I. Trade
item.description: The A I buildout's biggest risk is no longer money. It's permission. Two weeks in one: earnings proved the demand, then a midterm sweep put data-center permits in doubt, and the market dumped the suppliers while it bought the spenders. Factories kept hiring, the Fed may hike rates, Firefly landed a big engine deal, Starship tries a double catch Friday, and Nvidia's board is investigating its CEO.…

item.title: Anthropic Opens Its Books as A.I. Borrowers Crack
item.description: Is anyone actually making money on A I? Anthropic's newly public S-1 gives the first audited answer, and it's yes. But in the same week the neoclouds that borrow to build A I got hammered, a hot economy boxed in the Fed, and NASA turned the Moon race into a race to be ready. Who can pay for growth, who can't, and what it means for your portfolio and your job search.

item.title: Can You Pay for Your Own Growth? SpaceX, Meta and the Cost of A.I.
item.description: The A I boom doesn't have a demand problem. It has a paying-for-it problem. SpaceX reveals that A I is now its biggest business, Meta's cash flow turns negative, and power-equipment stocks tumble as rates sit near five percent. Plus: why electricity is the new A I bottleneck, what Anthropic's coming I P O could reset, and where the factory jobs are.
